title: First jazz records: Red Nichols, Indiana Five, Ellington's Washingtonians
summary: In his freshman year of high school early jazz records drew him in, including Red Nichols and Duke Ellington's eight-piece group that sounded like jungle music.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Growing up with radio, records and family listening

blocks.x: And then, when I got into high school, my freshman year, I became truly interested in -- via some early jazz records, and became involved that way.
Do you recall what some of those --

Yeah, some of the earliest things that were influencing me at the time were pieces played by such groups as the Indiana Five, Red Nichols, because I liked all the soloists that he was able to have on his records, and then I also -- one of the earliest records I had was Duke Ellington, when he had an eight-piece group known as the Washingtonians. And it sounded to me like jungle music. And I guess at some point it was even called a jungle band.
And I found this to be very exciting and very different from anything I had ever heard or felt, and so consequently I -- all these things made a big influence.
